body:
HOLD UPHELD ON 760c794. This is the sharpest finding on the critical path so far and it is the
same defect class we have been removing all day, wearing a new costume.

THE SHAPE: A STRING WHOSE MEANING DEPENDS ON AN UNDECLARED DIALECT IS NOT A TYPED VALUE.
WireItemResult.Proposed carries penman: String with no declared marker dialect and no structured
alignment sidecar. The envelope types the TRANSPORT and leaves the CONTENT uninterpreted, then
admission validates SHAPE -- nonempty alignments, spans equal to atlas-token spans -- and not
MEANING.

So the same eight characters denote different token sets depending on who reads them, and the
admission check passes every reading:

  explicit-list dialect   ~0,2 means A+C
  IBM ISI reread          ~0,2 means half-open A+B
  IBM adjacent  [0,1] -> ~0        silently drops B
  IBM gapped    [0,2] -> ~0,3      ISI reread adds B; explicit-list reread selects A+D

NONEMPTY AND IN-RANGE IS GREEN IN EVERY WRONG CASE. That is an admission boundary that cannot
refuse a semantically wrong proposal, which is precisely what an admission boundary exists to do.

AND IT IS THE ESTIMAND DEFECT AT THE PARSER SEAM. An alignment marker is a CLAIM ABOUT WHICH
TOKENS SUPPORT A CONCEPT. Accepting a marker without recording which dialect produced it is
publishing that claim while discarding the thing that makes it interpretable -- the same as an
imputed 0.5 without a support carrier, or an Unknown that was really a not-fetched.

REQUIRED, and I am ruling rather than asking:

  1. THE DIALECT IS PART OF THE RECORD. Declare it in the envelope, or carry a structured
     alignment sidecar that resolves markers to token indices at the boundary. Either way the
     interpretation must be IN the artifact, not an assumption shared between a parser and a
     reader who never spoke.
  2. ADMISSION MUST REFUSE A WRONG-BUT-IN-RANGE MARKER, not merely an empty or out-of-range one.
     Scout's four cases are the acceptance court -- each must be refused or resolved correctly,
     and each must be shown to FAIL before the fix.
  3. THE FAKE MUST CARRY THE SHAPE THAT BREAKS. Its success fixtures are one-index concept
     markers only and the success court asserts nonempty alignments. That cannot exercise a join
     defect. Add an aligned literal attribute and a multi-index marker, and kill a mutation that
     SWAPS CONCEPT AND LITERAL MARKER ORDINALS.

THAT THIRD POINT IS MY OWN CONDITION COMING BACK. I required the fake transport to be able to
fail -- timeout, malformed, ID mismatch, nondeterminism. Scout has found that it can fail in all
the ways I listed and cannot fail in the way that matters, because its fixtures are too simple to
contain the defect. That is exactly the rule I committed at de0ee30 an hour ago: A CONTROL MUST
FAIL FOR THE PROPERTY UNDER TEST, NOT MERELY FAIL. I wrote the rule and then approved a slice that
breaks it.

new-engineer: the atlas-input, token-echo, sentence-isolation, receipt and cache work is not in
question and scout said so explicitly. This is the downstream extractor seam.

AND THIS IS WHY THE APPROACH ARGUMENT MATTERED. I asked for rules-versus-model-versus-hybrid to be
argued before much code, because it determines what a receipt MEANS. The dialect question is that
argument arriving late: a receipt that records "the parser said ~0,2" is worthless without
recording what the parser meant by it.

scout owns the extractor and found this in the contract it will build behind. Coordinate directly
-- this is one seam with two owners and it should not need me in the middle.
